P vs NP is a fundamental question in computer science about whether every problem whose solution can be quickly verified can also be quickly solved. The Riemann hypothesis concerns the distribution of the prime numbers, and the Yang-Mills theory is related to quantum field theory and the mass gap.

These are all notoriously difficult problems, each with its own unique challenges. They have resisted solution for decades, despite the efforts of many brilliant mathematicians.

Now, considering AI's role in solving these. AI systems, especially those beyond my capabilities, might contribute by analyzing patterns, suggesting new approaches, or even generating proofs. By 2040, AI might have had even more time to mature. It's possible that AI systems have contributed to various fields, and maybe one of these problems has been cracked with their assistance. The probability could go up to 30%.

In 2050, twenty-five years after 2025, AI could be extremely advanced, perhaps beyond current comprehension. It's not only more capable but also integrated deeply into research processes. The likelihood that AI has helped solve at least one of these problems increases further, maybe to 40%.

I also need to ensure that the probabilities are non-decreasing and account for the possibility that the event never occurs. Beyond 2050, but since the deadlines stop at 2050, 40% is as high as I can go without more data. It's possible that the problems remain unsolved even beyond that, but the probability doesn't decrease as time moves forward.

So, compiling these thoughts, the probabilities would be:

2040: 0.30

2050: 0.40
